market_holds: Spot $1.36 (sealed baseline 2026-11-16 18:14 UTC), about $34M market cap on 25.08M shares at 2026-06-30 (own arithmetic). No option market and no usable reaction history in the baseline, so no implied move; 20d realised vol 98% gives a one-day band of about 6.2%. Run-in: -26.1% over 20 sessions and -2.9% over 5, -64% from the 52-week high, against IWM +0.5% and ONEW -3.9% over 20d (Yahoo). So most of the fall is the company's own. It lines up with its own financing news: a 15% 90-day bridge disclosed 2026-10-19 (stock -7% on 106k shares on 10-20), and a 12.99% revolver secured by the chairman's shares, priced off a 10-day VWAP of $1.905 (8-K 2026-10-29). The stock is about 29% below that VWAP now. It touched $1.00 intraday on 11-12 and closed 11-13 at $1.40 on 112k shares, the heaviest volume in a month. No usable consensus: one covering broker (the IPO underwriter, $10 target in January), aggregator EPS fields blank. The guide is FY2026 revenue of $165-170M, kept on 2026-08-13; with H1 at $88.9M that needs $76-81M in H2, against $61.3M in H2 2025. Turnover is about $49k a day. Insiders control roughly 45-50% of the votes (S-1).
view: A tiny, thinly traded, promotional boat broker and dealer that grew by acquisition. Its last reported quarter (Q2, released 2026-08-13 after the close) had record revenue of $59.1M (+88%) but a $2.1M net loss, after the chairman had said in July it expected to be 'at or near profitability'. The stock opened -4.8% the next morning. Since then the company has gone quiet on operations, after issuing operating-update releases every few weeks in the first half. What it has filed instead: a CEO change (2026-09-28); the CFO's resignation (notice 10-05, no successor named); a $510k convertible from a small lender at a 10% discount with a resetting conversion price (August); a 15% 90-day bridge that must be repaid from the equity in seven named pre-owned boats (October); a 12.99% revolver secured by the chairman's pledged shares; a related-party slip lease; and an S-1 for an offering assumed at $5 that has not priced. Inventory more than doubled to $60.4M at June 30, against a $60M floor-plan line, while the largest peer reported same-store sales -5.7% for July-September. That points to a weak Q3 on profit and cash. A new CEO with EBITDA-target options, presenting his first print while the CFO leaves, also has a reason to reset: cut or withdraw the guide, write down inventory or acquisition goodwill. Against that, revenue will probably look strong year on year off a soft $24.0M Q3 2025 base with the acquisitions included, and the company usually leads with that. The full-year revenue guide is reachable on simple seasonality. And the price already holds most of the liquidity stress: it is down about 29% since the financings, at roughly 0.23x trailing sales, so a print that only confirms losses could see a relief bid in a stock whose free float trades about $49k a day. On balance I lean modestly down: the risk of a reset by new management, and the company's silence where it used to pre-announce, are not fully in a price that has mostly reacted to the financings. But I cannot see the deciding line (whether the guide holds, the size of the loss, cash at September 30), and the opening print on a stock this thin is mostly noise.
unpriced: Possibly the chance that the new management team resets: withdraws or cuts the FY revenue guide, writes down inventory or acquisition goodwill, or adds liquidity warnings in the 10-Q. The price fell on the financing news. I cannot show that it holds a guide cut. Evidence is circumstantial and the gap is small relative to noise.

recommendation.reason: The downside lean rests on soft tells: management turnover, costly post-quarter financing, the absence of the operating pre-announcements the company made in Q2, and a new CEO's incentive to reset. Most of that stress is already in a stock down 26% in 20 sessions. Revenue growth will probably headline well, and the stock is thin enough that the open could go either way on a small order. Below the 65 bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: The FY2026 revenue guide of $165-170M reaffirmed or raised, with Q3 adjusted EBITDA positive and a concrete cost or profitability plan from the new CEO: that would likely produce a relief gap up from a depressed price.

self_critique: The stress is visible and has already been sold: the stock fell about 29% after the financings and sits near its lows at roughly 0.23x sales. A company that leads with revenue growth (likely +50% or more year on year off a soft Q3 2025) and reaffirms a reachable revenue guide could gap up on very thin volume. The Nov 13 high-volume rebound may show buyers positioning for exactly that. My downside tells (silence, turnover, incentives) are circumstantial, and new CEOs do not always reset in their first six weeks.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped: it showed the fall was the company's own and tied to dated financing news, which kept me from double-counting the liquidity stress. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' was hard to apply with no consensus and no counterparty data for a $34M broker; the absence of the company's usual pre-announcements was the most useful 'fresh since last spoke' signal.
